doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Fitting in with visiting singers; Wynonie Harris
summary: Jeannie explains how the house band bonded with singers; Wynonie Harris called her 'Miss Box' and told fortunes.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So you were in a house band and the singers would come through. And you’d just do your best to fit into their styles.

That was very easy for us because first of all we were very good musicians. Second of all, they would come in the night before they were supposed to open, and watch the other guy close. So we had a chance to talk to them you know, sit at the bar and hang out and talk. And so we’d connect with their attitude right away see. And in fact I was thinking about Jo Jones’ cousin was Wynonie Harris. That’s his first cousin. And Wynonie, when he rehearsed, he’d say, “Okay, play me a shuffle in B flat.” [brief scat]. “That’s enough. The rehearsal is over.” He called me “Miss Box.” Because he called the piano a box. He said “That’s Miss Box. Miss Box is here.” And then, sometimes at intermission he’d put this turban on. And he and our bass player would tell fortunes, and make extra money. Look, he was a very psychic person. He really could read. Wynonie Harris.
Very, very clairvoyant. And so was Shakespeare. So they used to sit and make extra money at intermission.
